findings.title: Making .small-action a flex container silently disables float: right on its button
findings.body: The PR adds `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action`, but the rule later in the same block still styles its `button { background: transparent; border: 0; float: right; }` (line 309). Children of a flex container become flex items and the `float` property is ignored on them, so the button (e.g. the banner/small-action close button) is no longer pushed to the right edge of the row. It will now render immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text, leaving a gap on the right and misplacing the control. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the container needs `justify-content: space-between`) to restore right alignment, as was done for `.panel` in header.scss. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), though there the flex row layout coincidentally produces a similar result.

findings.title: .panel right-alignment relies on margin-left: auto, which IE10 flexbox does not honor
findings.body: The new flexbox mixins explicitly target IE10 by emitting `display: -ms-flexbox` / `-ms-flex-align`, but the header's right-hand `.panel` is positioned purely via `margin-left: auto` (the old `float: right` was removed). IE10's flexbox implementation does not support auto margins for main-axis alignment (alignment there must be done with `-ms-flex-pack`), so on IE10 the search/hamburger/user panel will not be pushed to the right edge of the header and will instead sit directly next to the title. Since the whole point of the `-ms-` prefixes in the mixins is to support that browser, `.contents` needs an `-ms-flex-pack: end`-style fallback (or the panel needs a different mechanism) for the layout to hold there.

findings.title: -ms-align-items is not a real CSS property
findings.body: The `align-items()` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. No such property exists — the Microsoft-prefixed old-syntax property is `-ms-flex-align`, which the mixin already emits on the previous line. The `-ms-align-items` declaration is invalid and will be dropped by every browser; it also fails CSS linting and can mislead future readers into thinking it does something. It should be removed.

findings.title: align-items() mixin omits the -moz-box-align counterpart that flexbox()/order() imply
findings.body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, so the mixin set explicitly claims to support old-Gecko flexbox; but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align` line. Any browser that ends up using the `-moz-box` code path (the only one it is given) will get a flex container with no vertical alignment, so `.d-header .contents`, `.small-action`, and the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` would be laid out with the old default (stretch/start) instead of centered/baseline as intended. Either add `-moz-box-align` for symmetry or drop the `-moz-box` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` output, since the two halves of the vendor story currently contradict each other.
